ADVISORY_BODY: Monday's session was a genuine, broad bounce: the S&P 500 gained 0.70% to close at 7,676.77, recovering part of last week's losses even as it remains below the psychologically important 7,700 level (FXStreet; today's own pipeline JSON shows an identical 7,676.77, +53.09, +0.70% print, cross-validating the close). FMP's sector snapshot shows the gain was broad — 7 of 11 sectors higher, led by Real Estate (+1.30%), Consumer Cyclical (+1.13%), and Technology (+1.03%), with Communication Services the lone meaningful laggard (-1.17%). VIX eased further to 17.9 (-2.72%) per today's own data pull, though a secondary source (RS Trading Desk's Monday wrap) shows a somewhat higher, internally inconsistent 18.4-18.45 read — either way, a calm level. Pre-market futures are indicated modestly higher again (S&P +0.13% to +0.23% and Nasdaq +0.14% to +0.34% across TradingKey and a Monday-evening Yahoo snapshot; FXStreet separately expects the cash index to “open 0.4% higher”), with FXStreet's own technical read cautioning that this is “extending the consolidation that began in early August” rather than a confirmed trend reversal — resistance 7,780-7,800, support 7,700. Underneath the calm, the bond market is quietly repricing hawkish into tomorrow's FOMC decision: the 10-year yield has pushed back up to essentially 5.00% (FMP treasury-rates, Oct 26, up from 4.96% on Oct 22), and an unverified FXStreet sidebar headline (“Federal Reserve: December hike expectations — BNY”) raises the possibility markets are now entertaining a December hike rather than a cut — a claim this report could not independently confirm beyond that single teaser, but one directionally consistent with the yield move. Tomorrow is genuinely loaded: the FOMC decision lands Wednesday at 2pm ET (consensus still expects a hold per TradingKey), and Microsoft and Alphabet both report after the close the same day, with Amazon following Thursday — a true binary-risk pileup. Today's own BMO earnings slate already confirms a mixed bag: Boeing missed on EPS (-$0.34 vs -$0.255 est.) despite beating on revenue ($24.188B vs $23.950B est.), while Coca-Cola ($0.91 vs $0.881 est.), HCA Healthcare ($7.22 vs $6.65 est.), and SoFi ($0.18 vs $0.1623 est.) all beat cleanly on both lines; PayPal beat on EPS ($1.45 vs $1.31 est.) but missed on revenue ($8.584B vs $8.715B est.) — all figures from FMP's earnings-calendar. Visa and Robinhood are also scheduled to report this morning; neither had posted actual results as of this pull. Overseas, HSBC fell roughly 6.75% pre-market on a revenue miss ($18.62B vs $19.16B est.) and a startling EPS print ($0.42 vs $2.21 consensus) that looks driven by a one-time charge given pre-tax profit actually rose 32% y/y to $9.6B (TradingKey) — the EPS figure is presented as reported, unreconciled. The dominant single story remains Brazil: Lula won Sunday's runoff with 51.8% of the vote against Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2% — the first time a candidate has ever lost the first round and gone on to win a Brazilian presidential runoff, and a result prediction markets had bet against (Yahoo/TIKR, CNBC). Petrobras fell roughly 15% and MercadoLibre 12% on Monday on the news (Yahoo/TIKR), with the market reading a fourth Lula term as locking in the current leadership's capital-allocation approach at Petrobras — capex has more than doubled since 2022 while the dividend payout ratio fell from 94% to under 40% of free cash flow, compressing the forward P/E from roughly 4.5x to roughly 3.6x even after the drop (versus a five-year low of 1.5x in Jan. 2023). That rout has not stopped: today's FMP biggest-losers list shows XP Inc. down 48.36%, Banco Bradesco down 28.01%, StoneCo down 27.44%, Azul down 32.61%, and Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional down 22.73% — alongside leveraged Brazil ETFs (BRZU, UBR) down roughly 39% each, a reminder those vehicles amplify the move rather than add new information. No independent source in this pull could confirm the reported 10% Brazilian real decline some outlets flagged as “possible” rather than observed. Elsewhere, two genuinely bullish AI-infrastructure data points emerged: Celestica (CLS) reported Q3 revenue of $5.83B (+83% y/y) and non-GAAP EPS of $3.30 versus $1.58 a year earlier, both beating the top of prior guidance, and raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $21B with a first-ever 2027 target of $40B — shares were indicated up roughly 15.8% pre-market (TradingKey). Separately, Meta raised its planned equity financing to $97.5B (a $25B common stock offering at $625/share, up from $22.5B, plus $12.5B of mandatory convertible preferred and an ATM program of up to $60B) to fund AI-infrastructure buildout, with Nvidia committing to subscribe $3B of the raise and AMD and Broadcom expressing interest in up to $5B combined — a chipmaker-financed structure that reads as a genuine vote of confidence in AI capex demand, directly countering the “AI-capex-doubt” narrative that drove the Oct. 22 Nasdaq rout; Meta shares themselves were “largely flat” pre-market on the news (TradingKey). On the geopolitical front, nothing has resolved: the NYT and CNN both reportedly say (via a secondary Substack wrap, not independently verified here) that the US and Israel have developed plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms, with CNN citing officials saying action is “a question of when, not if”; Iran's IRGC claims four tankers were struck and three more hit mines near the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump disputes as Iran “making up fake hits and mines” to lift oil prices ahead of the midterms — neither claim is independently confirmed. Brent is indicated around $109.96-110/bbl and WTI around $100.71-101.40/bbl, essentially unchanged to modestly higher (TradingKey, RS Trading Desk). AAII's bull-bear spread sits at -8.9 (bulls 36.9%, bears 45.8%), unchanged from the week-ending-Oct.-21 reading and still below its historical average for a 14th straight week (AAII, published Oct. 24) — sentiment has not caught up to Monday's bounce.
